newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunis Air, Air France in cooperation talks.
newsitem.headline: Tunis Air, Air France in cooperation talks.

text.p: French airline Air France and Tunisia's company Tunis Air have started talks to strengthen cooperation to face changes in the world's air transport sector, Air France chairman said in remarks published on Monday.
"The two parties are preparing for the coming months a project for a partnership," Christian Blanc said in Tunis after a meeting with Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali over the weekend.
"The air transportation sector will see a big mutation during the next years, and the French and Tunisian companies must prepare the better possible complementarity between them," he added.
Air France has a minority five percent stake in the capital of Tunis Air which has flights to France's and European main airports.

The Tunisian state-controlled company has a capital of 53 million dinars. In 1995, it sold 20 percent of its capital for an amount of 32 million dinars in the biggest sell off in Tunisia's privatisation programme so far.
An additional sell off is planned for 1997.
It transported a total 2.697,712 million passengers in 1996, up by 4.26 percent from 2.587,529 million passengers in 1995.
Tunis Air was to replace its ageing seven Boeing-727 and two Boeing-737 in the next five years.
It has 24 planes from Airbus and Boeing models, including nine it bought during the last five years. ($1=1.1 dinar)
